title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Heparin infusion
decisions.scenario: A patient receiving a continuous heparin infusion has laboratory results indicating that the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is higher than the prescribed therapeutic range.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Adjust or hold infusion per protocol.

decisions.title: Medication error discovery
decisions.scenario: While reviewing documentation, a nurse realises that an incorrect medication dose was administered to a patient earlier in the shift. The patient currently shows no obvious signs of distress.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Ensure patient safety and report the error.

decisions.title: High-risk medication – chemotherapy
decisions.scenario: A nurse is preparing to administer chemotherapy medication as part of a patient’s cancer treatment regimen. The medication requires special handling, preparation, and verification due to its toxic nature.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Follow specialised handling and double-check protocols.

decisions.title: Medication and pregnancy
decisions.scenario: A pregnant patient is prescribed a medication during a routine antenatal visit. While reviewing the medication profile, the nurse recognises that the drug is known to be teratogenic.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Clarify the order with the prescriber.

decisions.title: Pediatric weight-based dosing
decisions.scenario: A medication order is written for a child, but the dose appears to be the same as an adult dose. The child’s weight is documented in the medical record but has not been used in dose calculation.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelWhy: Children are at high risk of dosing errors.

decisions.title: Elderly polypharmacy
decisions.scenario: An elderly patient taking multiple prescribed medications reports feeling dizzy and unsteady when standing. The patient has recently been started on a new medication in addition to existing therapies.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Medication refusal
decisions.scenario: A patient refuses to take a prescribed medication, stating concern about potential side effects after reading information online. The patient appears anxious and asks whether the medication is truly necessary.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Time-critical medication
decisions.scenario: A patient with Parkinson’s disease is scheduled to receive medication at a specific time to control symptoms. Due to workload delays, the medication administration time has already passed.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Administer medication as soon as possible.
